newsitem.title: UK: GUS up on 1 billion stg U.S. acquisition.
newsitem.headline: GUS up on 1 billion stg U.S. acquisition.

text.p: Great Universal Stores Plc shares rose in early trading on Thursday after the group said it was paying 1.05 billion stg for Experian, a Californian supplier of credit, marketing and real estate information services.
The stock, which on November 8 closed at a year's low of 583p, was up 13p at 603-1/2 at 0808 GMT.

"They seem to be paying a fairly full price in terms of Experian's earnings and sales, but the deal seems to have a certain amount of commercial logic," said William Cullum, an analyst at Paribas Capital Markets.

GUS said the move would be financed through an $800 million loan with the rest coming from its own existing resources. It said the acquisition would be earnings enhancing in the first full year of ownership.

In 1995 Experian made an operating profit of $87 million on sales of $540 million according to U.S. accounting standards, while under UK standards it made an operating profit of $109 million -- expected to rise to $114 million in 1996.

"It is a very positive acquisition by the look of it," said Roy Maconochie, an analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite. "It is earnings-enhancing, GUS has been sitting on over a billion pounds of cash and this is obviously going to enhance earnings in year one."
"Also it is strategically a good acquisition."

Maconochie pointed out that Experian would have $19 million in development costs in 1996, which would not recur in 1997, and that planned cost savings would give a further $11.4 million in a full year.
GUS chairman Lord Wolfson said Experian was a good fit with its existing CCN unit. "The geographic and product fits are excellent," he said.

"Experian and CCN together form a truly global business. Experian offers the databases, the customers and the technical platform through which to introduce CCN's value-added products in the U.S. market and vice versa."
Shares in Next Plc retreated as the GUS move was seen as making a long-rumoured bid for the fashion retailer less likely in the short-to-medium term.
Next shares were down 5p at 553 by 0735 GMT.
